sections.heading: C — Railroad crossings, light rail and bicyclists
sections.markdown:
## C — Railroad crossings, light rail and bicyclists

FACT_ID: sec13-F01 | anchor: A01
On a highway of five or more lanes with a shared center turn lane, vehicles in the lanes behind a stopped school bus must stop fully, while opposite-direction traffic is not legally required to. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec13-F02 | anchor: A01
Breaking school bus traffic laws carries serious legal consequences. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec13-F03 | anchor: A01
A train can reach a crossing at any hour, so approach with caution and obey every warning device, light, gate and sign. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec13-F04 | anchor: A01
At a crossing without flashing lights or gates, stop beforehand if needed to check for trains. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec13-F05 | anchor: A01
It is illegal and very dangerous to stop on the tracks; enter a crossing only once you know the rails are clear and your car fits fully past them, and with several tracks watch for a second train. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec13-F06 | anchor: A01
If your car stalls on the rails, have all occupants leave and move well away right away, train or no train in view, then phone the number on the blue Emergency Notification sign or local law enforcement. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec13-F07 | anchor: A01
A train's large size makes it look slower than it really is, and an average freight train at 55 mph needs about one mile to stop. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec13-F08 | anchor: A01
The round advance warning sign, the only round traffic sign, tells you a railroad crossing is ahead early enough for you to stop if needed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec13-F09 | anchor: A01
Railroad pavement markings show an R X R and a stop line; wait behind the line for a passing train, or at least 10 feet from the tracks if no line shows, because trains overhang the rails by 3 feet. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec13-F10 | anchor: A01
In a designated quiet zone a No Train Horn sign hangs below the advance warning sign, horns do not sound, and the flashing lights and gates are your warning. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec13-F11 | anchor: A01
Treat a crossbuck like a yield sign; a sign beneath it gives the number of tracks when there is more than one, and the crossbuck is normally a caution sign that becomes regulatory when a train approaches. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec13-F12 | anchor: A01
Commercial buses and hazardous-materials trucks must stop at most crossings, so be ready to stop when following one. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec13-F13 | anchor: A01
Always stop when crossing lights flash and do not cross until they stop flashing. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec13-F14 | anchor: A01
Where gates are used with flashing lights, the road is closed while the gates are down; wait until the gates rise and the lights stop flashing. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec13-F15 | anchor: A01
Every public highway-rail grade crossing has a blue Emergency Notification System sign, usually on the post below the crossbuck, with a phone number answered at all hours. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec13-F16 | anchor: A01
The ENS number is for emergencies that would require stopping a train, and giving the DOT crossing number on the sign lets the dispatcher pinpoint the crossing and warn trains. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec13-F17 | anchor: A01
RTD runs light rail vehicles in the Denver metro area, sometimes in the same direction as traffic and sometimes against it, and on streets they obey all signals and signs with the same rights and duties as other motorists. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec13-F18 | anchor: A01
A light rail car can weigh up to 40 tons and cannot stop quickly, so never turn in front of one or across its tracks without checking every direction. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec13-F19 | anchor: A01
Watch for riders getting on and off a stopped light rail vehicle, and stay alert because buildings and plants can hide light rail vehicles. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec13-F20 | anchor: A02
Light rail crossings may use regular traffic lights, warning lights or gates with arms, and all of them mean stop and do not cross the tracks. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec13-F21 | anchor: A02
Never drive around light rail gates, even right after a train passes, because another may be coming from the other direction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec13-F22 | anchor: A02
Light rail overhead wires sit at a standard 18 feet, 6 inches above the track center, so know your vehicle height, assume any hanging wire is live and never touch it or anything touching it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec13-F23 | anchor: A02
Report a hanging overhead wire or faulty light rail safety device by calling 911 or RTD. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec13-F24 | anchor: A02
Bicycles are vehicles on the roadway, and their riders generally follow the same rules of the road with many of the same rights and duties as motorists. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec13-F25 | anchor: A02
Some local ordinances treat bicyclists differently, for example letting them ride on sidewalks and in crosswalks with pedestrian rights and duties. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec13-F26 | anchor: A02
Bicyclists are smaller and more vulnerable than people in vehicles and vary in skill, and some are children, so look for them actively and use caution when approaching or passing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec13-F27 | anchor: A02
Bicyclists should ride as far right as they judge safe, but they may take the center of the lane for visibility, on narrow roads, or to avoid car door zones, broken glass or drainage grates. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec13-F28 | anchor: A02
When passing a bicyclist, even one in a bike lane, give at least three feet from the outermost part of your vehicle or attachments; if you cannot, slow down and stay behind until it is safe. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec13-F29 | anchor: A02
Crossing a double yellow line with no oncoming traffic is legal when needed to give a bicyclist the three-foot passing gap. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec13-F30 | anchor: A02
Bicyclists may ride side by side when they are not blocking normal, reasonable traffic flow, which can make them more visible and quicker to pass. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec13-F31 | anchor: A02
Yield to bicyclists in intersections as you would to pedestrians and other vehicles. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec13-F32 | anchor: A02
Bicyclists have the right-of-way in a bike lane, the lane continues through intersections even without paint, and drivers may not stop, park or drive in a bike lane or path. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec13-F33 | anchor: A02
To avoid the common left-turn crash with an oncoming cyclist, look for riders on the shoulder, at the lane edge or behind other vehicles and judge their speed and distance before turning. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec13-F34 | anchor: A02
To avoid stop-sign and signal crashes, stop first, then enter the intersection only after looking for and yielding to others. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec13-F35 | anchor: A02
Before opening a door into the roadway, check behind for passing riders or vehicles, and try opening it with the hand farther from the door. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec13-F36 | anchor: A02
When turning right, yield and let a cyclist going straight clear the intersection first, and turn from close to the curb so no rider can pass unsafely on your right. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec13-F37 | anchor: A02
When pulling out of a driveway, check both directions and past the curb or driveway for riders on the road, sidewalk or bike path. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0025]
